sections.dimensions:
The business process is retail order-item sales. Following Kimball’s four steps, the design selects the process, declares one original order item as the grain, identifies dimensions and defines measures (Kimball Group, n.d.-a). A consistent grain prevents accidental mixing of order totals and item-level measures (Kimball Group, n.d.-b).

FactSales preserves a unique OrderItemID, while SalesKey is its surrogate primary key. OrderID and ItemSequence are degenerate identifiers. Six required foreign keys connect Customer, Product, Seller, purchase Date and two roles of Geography. Customer contains exact source age, gender and integrated education. Product flattens category and subcategory into one dimension, avoiding a snowflake. Seller retains registration information, including the original textual end date. Date uses a YYYYMMDD key with year, quarter, month and day. Geography distinguishes customer destinations from seller origins through GeographyRole and a unique role-location pair. These dimensions support demographic, regional, product and annual supplier comparisons (Kimball & Ross, 2013).

The transaction snapshot contains 137,901 facts, 21,000 customers, 2,199 products, 100 sellers, 493 dates and 1,599 geography rows. Geography includes 1,500 customer locations and 99 distinct seller locations. One seller-location ID has conflicting TAS and WA mappings; its state is explicitly UNK and contradictory details are null, while both original CSV records remain preserved.

Additive quantity and LineAmount support the required queries. UnitSalesPrice is a unit-rate measure, so it must not be summed as revenue. Source floats remain available alongside four-decimal amounts, recomputed extended amount and the difference from the supplied line total. Missing freight remains null. All order statuses are retained, but delivered orders form the completed-sales proxy. No source costs establish profit, and no history supports Type 2 changes. This is a snapshot warehouse, not an inferred historical record.
sections.implementation:
The SSIS master package resets only the allowlisted student warehouse, then runs eleven Data Flow Tasks in success order. Four Flat File Source flows preserve the complete age, education, state and seller-location CSV records. OLE DB Source queries project original operational fields; native Lookup transformations integrate references and assign dimension keys. Derived Column transformations normalise education codes, create date attributes and calculate measures, while Data Conversion enforces destination types (Microsoft, n.d.).

Product joins its subcategory and category through Lookups. Geography resolves customer states and masks the contradictory seller location before a native Sort removes the duplicate transformed location. The date flow derives calendar fields and sorts to one row per date. FactSales looks up order attributes and six dimension roles, retaining unmatched-row failure dispositions. Native Row Count components record each destination count.

Direct conversion from floating-point amounts originally truncated some fourth-decimal values. The corrected Derived Column expressions round scaled amounts to integral ten-thousandths, then use exact numeric division. Raw floats remain unchanged for audit. Fast-load destinations enable CHECK_CONSTRAINTS, and the reset validates and restores constraint trust. No SQL joins or INSERT SELECT statements load warehouse data.

Counts, source-field comparisons, monetary checks and relationship tests accompany execution. Actual backup restoration passed CHECKDB, full-row comparisons for ten tables and the four reproduced query results.
